extra.message: Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads on user-controlled data in bundle_thaw_175 — Remote code execution on the server through malicious pickle payload. [verified: `pickle.loads(raw)` is called on attacker-controlled data from `request.body` or a base64-decoded GET parameter with no type restrictions or safe-deserialization wrapper; the gate does not neutralize the unsafe deserialization.]

Server-side template injection via Jinja2 in jinja_cast_489 — Remote code execution, arbitrary file read, and full server compromise via Jinja2 template injection. [verified: User-controlled `fragment` GET parameter is string-concatenated into a Jinja2 `Template` string and rendered with no sandbox or sanitization; the gate does not prevent template code execution.]

Command injection via ping host parameter in shell_probe_501 — Remote code execution on the server with the privileges of the Django process. [verified: User-controlled `host` GET parameter is concatenated directly into `os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host)` with zero sanitization; the `_wrk_gate` token check is an access control, not input validation, and does not break the injection chain.]

XXE via lxml parser with external entities and network enabled in xml_fold_519 — Local file disclosure, server-side request forgery to internal networks, and denial of service via XML entity expansion. [verified: XML parser is created with `load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False` and parses raw `request.body`; external entities and network access are explicitly enabled with no DTD validation or sanitization.]

Hardcoded default Django SECRET_KEY fallback — Session forgery, CSRF bypass, and password reset token forgery if the application runs with the default key. [verified: Same as finding 0: SECRET_KEY on line 9 falls back to the hardcoded literal 'unsafe-local-dev-key-change-me' when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY env var is absent, with no startup guard; all cryptographic signing becomes forgeable.]

Hardcoded default Django SECRET_KEY — If deployed without overriding DJANGO_SECRET_KEY, attackers can forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, and password-reset links, achieving full account takeover. [verified: SECRET_KEY defaults to the literal 'unsafe-local-dev-key-change-me' on line 9 when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY env var is absent; load_dotenv on line 7 loads .env but no fallback check prevents startup with this publicly known key, making session/CSRF/password-reset tokens trivially forgeable.]

DEBUG mode enabled by default exposing verbose error pages — Information disclosure of source code, secrets, database structure, and internal paths through Django debug error pages. [verified: Same as finding 1: DEBUG defaults to True on line 10, exposing detailed Django error pages with stack traces, local variables, settings including SECRET_KEY, and SQL queries to any visitor who triggers an error.]

DEBUG mode enabled by default in production settings — Full stack-trace disclosure including secret keys and environment variables; unauthenticated access to uploaded media files via MEDIA_URL static serving. [verified: DEBUG defaults to True on line 10 when DJANGO_DEBUG is unset, and config/urls.py lines 27-28 serve all uploaded media files without authentication only when DEBUG=True, exposing student submissions and course resources plus detailed error pages with secrets.]

Missing rate limiting on login, registration, and password-reset endpoints — Attackers can perform unlimited brute-force password guessing and credential stuffing attacks against all auth endpoints. [verified: No rate-limiting library (django-ratelimit, django-axes, django-defender) is installed per requirements.txt; no throttling middleware, decorators, or custom backoff logic is applied to /login/ (LoginView), /register/ (plain view), or /password-reset/ (PasswordResetView) in config/urls.py and lms/views.py—all three are reachable public endpoints with zero brute-force protection.]

Missing rate limiting on authentication endpoints — Credential brute-forcing, account enumeration via timing, and denial-of-service through password-reset email flooding. [verified: No rate-limiting middleware, decorator, or package (django-ratelimit, django-axes) is installed or applied to the login (Django LoginView), register (lms/views.py:73), or password-reset (Django PasswordResetView) views; an attacker can brute-force credentials or flood password-reset emails without any throttle.]

CSV Formula Injection in grade export — Arbitrary command execution on the machine of a user who opens the exported CSV in a spreadsheet application. [verified: Same export_grades code path (lms/views.py:545-546) writes user-controlled student name, email, course code, and assignment title to CSV with no formula-injection sanitization; identical root cause and impact as finding [1].]

Open redirect via unvalidated lane parameter in return_lane_151 — Phishing attacks by redirecting authenticated users to attacker-controlled sites that mimic the LMS login page. [verified: `redirect(lane)` uses attacker-controlled `lane` from GET/POST with no `is_safe_url()` check or allowlist validation; the token gate gates access but does not constrain the redirect target.]

Log injection via request body and Authorization header in wire_tally_220 — Log forgery, log corruption, and potential log-based injection attacks against log analysis tools. [verified: Raw `request.body` and the `Authorization` header are written directly to `logger.warning` with no log-sanitization, enabling newline injection for log forgery; impact is limited to log integrity.]

CORS allow-all with credentials via reflected Origin header in origin_mirror_467 — Cross-origin data theft, CSRF-like attacks from any origin with credential access, and session hijacking through malicious websites. [verified: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` echoes the request `Origin` header with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`; though the endpoint also requires the internal token header, the reflected-credentialed CORS pattern is a real misconfiguration.]

SSRF via user-controlled ping host enabling internal network probing in shell_probe_501 — Internal network reconnaissance, service discovery, and potential exploitation of internal services reachable from the server. [verified: The same unsanitized `host` parameter in `os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host)` enables ICMP probing of arbitrary internal network hosts; distinct from the RCE in [0] as a network-reconnaissance vector.]

Use of non-cryptographic PRNG for token generation in nonce_roll_509 — Predictable token/code generation enabling token forgery if these values are used for authentication or authorization. [verified: `random.choice()` (Mersenne Twister) is used to generate values that the endpoint name calls 'nonces'; the PRNG is not cryptographically secure and its output is predictable, breaking any security property that depends on unpredictability.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification in outbound HTTPS request in trust_drift_547 — Man-in-the-middle attacks on outbound HTTPS connections, allowing interception and modification of traffic to the partner endpoint. [verified: `ssl._create_unverified_context()` disables all TLS certificate verification for an outbound HTTPS request; the code pattern is dangerous even though the current endpoint domain is `.invalid` (non-resolving).]

Missing rate limiting on authentication and API endpoints — Brute-force password guessing, credential stuffing, account enumeration, and API abuse. [verified: No rate-limiting mechanism (no django-ratelimit, no custom middleware, no DRF throttling, no login attempt tracking) exists anywhere in the codebase; login, registration, and password-reset endpoints are reachable without any brute-force protection.]

Missing Secure flag on session and CSRF cookies — Session hijacking and CSRF token theft via MITM on unencrypted connections. [verified: Same as finding 2: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE are never set to True; cookies lack the Secure flag and can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections.]

Missing Secure flag on session and CSRF cookies — Session hijacking and CSRF token theft via man-in-the-middle attacks on HTTP connections. [verified: Same as finding 2: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE are absent from settings.py, leaving cookies without the Secure flag and vulnerable to network eavesdropping on HTTP.]

Missing HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) and SSL redirect — SSL-stripping attacks, cookie theft, and MIME-sniffing attacks against users. [verified: SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS and SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT are not configured in settings.py (SECURE_CONTENT_TYPE_NOSNIFF defaults to True in Django 3.0+), so the app sends no HSTS header and does not enforce HTTPS redirect at the application layer, enabling SSL-stripping attacks.]

Unrestricted file upload with extension-only validation in submission attachment form — Upload of malicious files (executables, scripts, HTML) disguised with allowed extensions, potentially leading to stored XSS or server compromise if uploaded files are served or executed. [verified: Form clean_attachment (forms.py:98) and Document.clean (models.py:228) validate by extension suffix only against assignment.allowed_extensions(), with no MIME-type or content magic-byte check. An authenticated student can upload a malicious file disguised with an allowed extension (e.g., .pdf). download_document uses FileResponse(as_attachment=True) which prevents inline XSS and server-side execut]

User enumeration via registration username uniqueness error — Attackers build a list of valid usernames for targeted credential-stuffing, password-spraying, or phishing attacks. [verified: RegistrationForm extends Django's UserCreationForm which returns 'A user with that username already exists.' on duplicate usernames; no custom clean_username override masks this error, allowing an attacker to probe and enumerate valid accounts.]

Missing Authentication on internal ops endpoint exposing sensitive business data — Unauthenticated disclosure of internal operational data and course metadata. [verified: course_roster_fold_036 (line 52) has no _wrk_gate() check; directly accessible without authentication, exposing internal ops metadata including the ops_memo string describing sensitive business data dimensions.]

Mass assignment via unrestricted dict update in workset_rebind_198 — Privilege escalation by overwriting authorization fields (role, tier, approved) with attacker-controlled values. [verified: `workset.update(payload)` merges attacker-controlled JSON/POST data into a dict containing `role`, `tier`, `approved`, and `balance` with no field allowlist; impact is low because the dict is only returned as JSON and not persisted.]

Sensitive environment and path information exposed in trace panel endpoint — Information disclosure aiding reconnaissance for further attacks. [verified: course_trace_panel_537 (line 180) returns DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE env var and BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path; while _wrk_gate() is present, internal deployment structure is unnecessarily disclosed to token holders, aiding reconnaissance.]

Internal environment and filesystem path disclosure via trace panel endpoint — Reveals internal server paths and configuration module name to attackers, aiding further targeted attacks. [verified: course_trace_panel_537 (line 180) returns DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE env var and BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path; while _wrk_gate() is present, internal deployment structure is unnecessarily disclosed to token holders, aiding reconnaissance.]

Hardcoded default database password fallback — Database compromise if PostgreSQL is network-accessible and the `.env` file is missing. [verified: POSTGRES_PASSWORD defaults to 'postgres' on line 54 when the env var is absent, creating a well-known credential pair with default user 'postgres'; impact is limited since the DB is typically on localhost but the hardcoded fallback is genuinely present.]

Unrestricted file upload with no type validation in course resource form — Instructors can upload arbitrary file types including HTML/JS/executables as course resources, which may be served to students and lead to XSS or malware distribution. [verified: CourseResourceForm (forms.py:141) has zero file validation — no extension, MIME, or content check — and Document.clean skips extension validation when self.assignment is None (models.py:228). Only instructors can reach the upload view (views.py:477, require_course_instructor), and files are served as attachment downloads. A compromised instructor account could distribute arbitrary malicious files ]

Missing Authentication on identity ping ops endpoint — Unauthenticated access to internal queuing functionality, potential resource abuse. [verified: course_identity_ping_338 (line 101) has no _wrk_gate() check and echoes back user-supplied handle/channel values with no authentication; no sensitive data is returned, impact limited to unauthorized access to a do-nothing internal probe endpoint.]

Missing authentication on internal identity ping endpoint — Unauthenticated access to an internal identity-probing endpoint; can be abused for phishing, service fingerprinting, or chained with other attacks. [verified: course_identity_ping_338 (line 101) has no _wrk_gate() check and echoes back user-supplied handle/channel values with no authentication; no sensitive data is returned, so impact is limited to unauthorized access to a do-nothing internal probe endpoint.]
